integrity: The upper bound comes from an explicit universal-pair labeling. For the lower bound, if both sides contain zeros then each opposite side must contribute at least three units; equality forces exactly one label 3 per side. One-sided-zero and all-positive regimes exceed weight six when both parts have size at least three. Equality then forces the two label-3 vertices to be universal.
scientific_limitations: Both bipartition classes are assumed to have size at least three.
Chain graphs with a side of size one or two are excluded because additional low-weight cases occur.
Finite exhaustive verification covers canonical chain types with side sizes three and four and is corroborative only.
A differently phrased or non-indexed chain-graph theorem may exist.
title: Minimum total double Roman functions of connected chain graphs
